title: Background, deployment, and architecture in one screen
rememberThis: BackgroundService is singleton — IServiceScopeFactory.CreateScope per message/batch, never inject DbContext directly.
Outbox pattern: order + outbox row in one SaveChanges; dispatcher publishes to SQS — no dual-write gap.
SQS is at-least-once — idempotent consumers, visibility timeout > processing time, DLQ for poison messages.
WebApplicationFactory + TestServer for integration tests; fake IEventPublisher; Testcontainers for real SQL.
REST public, gRPC internal — shared Application handlers; browsers cannot call gRPC natively.
bullets: Co-host light workers (outbox dispatcher); split CPU-heavy jobs to dedicated Worker Service container.
Bounded Channel<T> with Wait mode for in-process backpressure; unbounded channel risks OOM.
Docker: SDK stage build → aspnet runtime stage; /health/live (self) vs /health/ready (DB tagged).
Clean Architecture: Domain pure C# → Application ports/handlers → Infrastructure EF/SQS → thin API.
K8s: readinessProbe on /health/ready removes pod from LB; livenessProbe lightweight — never check DB on liveness.
Integration test outbox: POST /orders → assert OutboxMessages row with ProcessedAt null before dispatcher runs.
